items.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: maths student, chess fan and Manchester City’s new Rodri
items.summary: The £85m midfielder passed his exams a year early, is studying for a degree and is ready to tackle Premier League learning curve “He’s like a computer,” the former Lille head of academy recruitment Mathieu Frison says of the £85m Manchester City recruit Ayyoub Bouaddi. “You teach him something, he learns it and can do it immediately.” Bouaddi has the mountainous challenge at his new club of replacing the best central midfielder in the world. It would be difficult for any player but at 18 years old it feels monumental, although those who know the Morocco international best would not bet against him. Bouaddi has known only Lille and Ligue 1 but is entering one of the biggest clubs in the world where a season without a trophy is deemed a failure. For someone so young, however, he has plenty of experience. He made his European debut three days after his 16th birthday and has played three full seasons in the first team, culminating in a place at the World Cup this summer. Continue reading...

items.title: Chelsea in talks with Emiliano Martínez’s camp after being offered goalkeeper
items.summary: Experienced World Cup winner wants to leave Aston Villa Sánchez errors at Fulham led to Chelsea conceding Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez and are considering making an offer for the goalkeeper. Martínez has told Aston Villa he wants to leave but a move to Juventus collapsed last week after Villa had signed his replacement, Zion Suzuki, from Parma for £30m. Goalkeeper has been a problematic position for Chelsea in recent seasons, with Robert Sánchez mainly the No 1 but prone to mistakes. Mike Penders, 21, is being lined up to become the first-choice keeper, but the new Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, selected Sánchez for Monday’s win against Fulham and two Sánchez errors led to goals. Continue reading...

items.summary: Uefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino plan European sides likely to go to under-20 Women’s World Cup Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table. items.title: Bristol City ready to ‘supercharge growth’ and prove women’s clubs can fly solo
items.summary: After a split from the men’s team, CEO Hannah Buckley is overseeing an ambitious rebuild with WSL promotion firmly in sight As radiant, August sunshine glistens around a peacefully silent Ashton Gate before Bristol City Women’s pre-season media day, Hannah Buckley takes a seat, pitch side, with a gleam in her eye, surveying the scene. The sight of a top-class venue makes her beam in a way that perhaps only somebody whose CV includes job titles such as regional facilities manager and head of infrastructure, safety and sustainability can. Nice stadiums, particular ones used by women’s sports teams, give her a kick. But after more than 20 years in football, the past eight at the WSL, Buckley is working on building something rather different: a club capable of thriving independently from the auspices of a men’s club. She was appointed as the Women’s Super League 2 side’s chief executive in May, starting her role in June, at a fascinating time in the team’s history, after they were taken over by the investment group Mercury13 last year to break away from the Bristol Sport group that oversees Bristol City’s men’s team and the city’s rugby union and basketball sides. Continue reading...

items.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
items.summary: Celtic lose against Lask in qualifier from 4-0 up on aggregate ‘That’s my team and that’s my responsibility,’ O’Neill says Martin O’Neill has admitted that Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager. Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion. Continue reading...

items.title: OFFICIEL : la RAAL se sépare de l’un des artisans de son retour dans l’élite du football belge
items.summary: Mohamed Guindo quitte officiellement la RAAL et rejoint le FC Aarau, formation de deuxième division suisse. Le Malien avait été prêté à Clermont Foot en deuxième partie de saison lors du dernier exercice. Il avait rejoint les Loups en juillet 2024 et quitte le club avec 44 apparitions à son actif. Sous les couleurs louviéroises, le natif de Bamako a inscrit huit buts et délivré trois assists.

items.title: OFFICIEL : Vincent Kompany voit l'un de ses joueurs quitter le Bayern
items.summary: C'est officiel, João Palhinha quitte le Bayern Munich et rejoint Benfica, où il a paraphé un contrat jusqu'en juin 2030. Vincent Kompany perd ainsi l'un de ses joueurs. La saison dernière, le Portugais avait été prêté à Tottenham par le Bayern.

items.title: Standard schakelt snel en wil uitpakken met opvallende terugkeer
items.summary: Standard lijkt snel te schakelen nu Dennis Eckert Ayensa op weg is naar Gençlerbirliği. De Rouches hebben hun oog laten vallen op Andi Zeqiri, een oude bekende op Sclessin. De 27-jarige spits staat momenteel onder contract bij het Poolse Widzew Lodz, maar een terugkeer naar België wordt onderzocht.

items.title: L'UEFA va lever sa menace de boycott de la Coupe du monde
items.summary: L’UEFA, la Concacaf et l’AFC ont publié une lettre ouverte s'adressant directement au monde du football. Via ce communiqué, les trois institutions répondent notamment à la récente lettre de la FIFA reconnaissant avoir commis des erreurs concernant son projet de vente de parts du Mondial.

items.title: Pourquoi maintenant et pour une si faible indemnité ? Les raisons du départ de Dennis Ayensa du Standard
items.summary: Dennis Ayensa est en train de quitter le Standard pour prendre la route de Gençlerbirliği, en Turquie, contre un petit million d'euros. Si l'indemnité du transfert peut paraître faible, elle s'explique notamment par la réalité financière et contractuelle du club du bord de Meuse, qui se doit de ne plus seulement avoir une vision à court terme et de continuer à diminuer sa masse salariale.

items.title: Heeft Antwerp nieuw goudhaantje gevonden? Nieuw 18-jarig talent loopt al rond op de Bosuil

items.title: Dit seizoen al goed voor twee doelpunten: Standard ziet aanvaller na twee seizoenen vertrekken
items.summary: Dennis Eckert Ayensa staat op het punt Standard opnieuw te verlaten. De 29-jarige spits is dicht bij een definitieve transfer naar Gençlerbirliği SK, waar een contract voor twee seizoenen met een optie op een extra jaar klaarligt. Voor de Rouches betekent zijn vertrek een opvallende aderlating, want Eckert Ayensa stond dit seizoen telkens in de basis en vond al twee keer de weg naar doel.
